title: Weierstrass models and singular points for Tate's algorithm
abstract: Formalizes Weierstrass models of elliptic curves over a commutative ring, their b- and c-invariants and discriminant, the change-of-coordinates group action, the discriminant's membership in the Jacobian ideal, and the construction of the singular point of a singular model over a perfect field, together with the Kronecker symbol and the Kodaira type enumeration.

informal.Model: Defines a Weierstrass model of a possibly singular elliptic curve by its five a-invariants.
informal.Model.discr_identity: Proves the identity relating the discriminant to the c-invariants, 1728 * discr = c4^3 - c6^2.
informal.Model.rst_discr: Proves that the discriminant is invariant under the rst change-of-coordinates transformation.
informal.Model.discr_in_jacobian_ideal: Expresses the discriminant as an explicit combination of the Weierstrass polynomial and its partial derivatives, witnessing membership in the Jacobian ideal.
informal.Model.discr_eq_zero_of_singular: Proves that a model with a singular point has vanishing discriminant.
informal.Model.Field.isSingularPoint_singularPoin: Proves that the explicitly constructed singular point of a singular model over a perfect field is indeed a singular point (Connell, Proposition 1.5.4).
informal.Model.Field.move_singular_point_to_origi: Proves that the change of coordinates moving the singular point places it at the origin.
informal.Kodaira: Enumerates the Kodaira reduction types, including the extra types arising over imperfect residue fields of characteristic 2 or 3.
